question: After the lifecycle defect is fixed, should OpenClaw adopt deny-over-allow through both `openclaw.json` and persisted exec approvals, including fail-closed node policy lookup?
rationale: The PR creates a new command-authorization boundary and operator-facing config contract, intentionally changing permissive exec behavior and lookup failure handling; code correctness alone cannot choose those security and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Adopt both surfaces
options.body: Land after current-denylist revalidation, upgrade proof, and explicit security-owner approval are complete.

options.title: Use approvals-file only
options.body: Remove `tools.exec.denylist` and keep deny policy under the existing persisted exec approvals owner to reduce duplicate state and freshness complexity.

options.title: Pause denylist support
options.body: Defer the feature if the added security and availability contract is not worth the lifecycle complexity.

recommendation.title: Adopt both surfaces
recommendation.body: Land after current-denylist revalidation, upgrade proof, and explicit security-owner approval are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current authorization revalidation framework and have the strongest current-main provenance across the affected policy paths.
